{{Short description|American bioscientist (1950–2024)}}
{{Use mdy dates|date=August 2025}}
'''Donald A. Bryant''' (March 12, 1950 – August 28, 2024)<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.kochfuneralhome.com/obituaries/Dr-Donald-A-Bryant?obId=33287908|title=Dr. Donald A. Bryant|work=Koch Funera Home|date=September 16, 2024}}</ref> was an American bioscientist. He was the [[Ernest C. Pollard|Ernest Pollard]] Chair of Biotechnology at the [[Eberly College of Science]]<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://science.psu.edu/about/honors/endowed |title=Holders of Endowed Chairs |publisher=science.psu.edu |accessdate=August 22, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160913182910/http://science.psu.edu/about/honors/endowed |archive-date=September 13, 2016 |url-status=dead }}</ref> [[Pennsylvania State University]]. He published numerous research publications which are widely cited.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=2tT-FokAAAAJ&hl=en |title=Donald A. Bryant |accessdate=August 22, 2016}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.worldcat.org/identities/lccn-n94092993/ |title=Bryant Donald A. |publisher=worldcat.org |accessdate=August 22, 2016}}</ref> Bryant's significant contributions include elucidating the key mechanisms of bacterial photosynthesis and the physiology of [[Chlorophototroph|chlorophototrophic]] microbes. His pioneering work provided deep insights into microbial light-harvesting systems and their ecological significance.<ref name=":1">{{Cite journal |last=Gisriel |first=Christopher J. |last2=Schluchter |first2=Wendy M. |last3=Gan |first3=Fei |last4=Golbeck |first4=John H. |last5=Ho |first5=Ming-Yang |last6=Shen |first6=Gaozhong |last7=Soulier |first7=Nathan T. |last8=Thiel |first8=Vera |last9=Ward |first9=David M. |last10=Zhao |first10=Jindong |last11=Zhang |first11=Shuyi |date=2025 |title=Remembering Don Bryant (1950–2024) |url=https://link.springer.com/10.1007/s11120-025-01158-1 |journal=Photosynthesis Research |language=en |volume=163 |issue=4 |doi=10.1007/s11120-025-01158-1 |issn=0166-8595 |pmc=12214013}}</ref>

== Professional career ==
* Earned a bachelor's degree in chemistry with honors at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] (1972), earned doctoral degree in molecular biology [[University of California, Los Angeles|UCLA]] (1977)<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |date=2024-12-18 |title=Penn State BMB department remembers Professor Emeritus Don Bryant {{!}} Penn State University |url=https://www.psu.edu/news/eberly-college-science/story/penn-state-bmb-department-remembers-professor-emeritus-don-bryant |access-date=2026-02-26 |website=www.psu.edu}}</ref> studying the phycobiliproteins of cyanobacteria.<ref name=":1" />
* Supported by a [[National Science Foundation|U.S. National Science Foundation]]/National Council for Scientific Research postdoctoral fellowship at the [[Pasteur Institute]] (1979)<ref name=":0" />
* Supported by a [[United States Department of Energy National Laboratories|Department of Energy]] postdoctoral research fellowship at [[Cornell University]] (1981)<ref name=":0" />
* Joined the [[Pennsylvania State University|Penn State]] faculty in 1981,  appointed the Ernest C. Pollard Professor of Biotechnology (1992)<ref name=":0" />
* Adjunct research appointment at [[Montana State University]] ( 2009-2020)<ref name=":0" /> 
* Visiting professor in the Singapore Centre on Environmental Life Sciences Engineering at [[Nanyang Technological University]]  (2013 -2018)<ref name=":0" />
* Published nearly 450 scientific papers, mentored 86 graduate students and 38 postdoctoral researchers<ref>{{Cite web |title=In memoriam: Donald A. Bryant |url=https://www.asbmb.org/asbmb-today/people/021025/in-memoriam-donald-a-bryant |access-date=2026-02-26 |website=www.asbmb.org |language=en}}</ref>

== Research ==
Bryant's research focused on understanding photosynthesis in two distinct groups of bacteria. [[Cyanobacteria]] produce oxygen as a photosynthetic byproduct. In contrast, he also researched [[green sulfur bacteria]] which are [[Anaerobic digestion|anaerobic]] and can survive only in the absence of oxygen.  

Bryant authored the book, The Molecular Biology of Cyanobacteria (1994)<ref>{{Cite book |last=Bryant |first=D. A. |url=https://books.google.co.uk/books?id=gZelQWTwxyQC |title=The Molecular Biology of Cyanobacteria |date=1995-02-28 |publisher=Springer |isbn=978-0-7923-3222-0 |language=en}}</ref> which summarizes  and analyzes the taxonomy, biochemistry, physiology, cellular differentiation and developmental biology of cyanobacteria, which was relatively understudied at the time.

* Charles F. Kettering Award in Photosynthesis from the American Society of Plant Biologists 2020<ref name=":2" />

* Daniel R. Tershak Memorial Teaching Award from the Penn State Department of Biochemistry and Molecular Biology 2010<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-09-01 |title=Penn State microbiologist’s estate gift to establish new chair and lectureship {{!}} Penn State University |url=https://www.psu.edu/news/eberly-college-science/story/penn-state-microbiologists-estate-gift-establish-new-chair-and |access-date=2026-03-04 |website=www.psu.edu}}</ref>
* Elected as a fellow of the American Academy of Microbiology 1995

* Elected member of the Board of Governors of the American Academy of Microbiology from 2012 - 2018
* Served on editorial boards for multiple journals including ''Journal of Bacteriology'', ''Photosynthesis Research'', ''Archives of Microbiology'', ''Journal of Biological Chemistry'' and ''Frontiers of Microbiology'',<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |title=Donald A. Bryant, Ph.D. |url=https://asm.org/biographies/donald-a-bryant,-ph-d |access-date=2026-02-26 |website=ASM.org |language=en}}</ref>
